title: 2024 Riverview Legal Studies Trial
notes: The trial paper contains no answer key and online searches surfaced the paper but no answer sheet. Answers are reasoned guesses. Q5–6 share a scenario; Q16’s single-question scenario is included in its stem. No figures occur in Section I.

groups.stimulus: Both the Commonwealth and New South Wales Parliament pass laws to protect the human rights of the disabled. The federal law conflicts with state legislation.

questions.stem: What is the difference between a summary and an indictable offence?
questions.answerNote: The classification primarily reflects the seriousness of the offence.

questions.stem: Which of the following should be considered a mitigating factor in sentencing an offender for assault?

options.A: The old age of the victim
options.D: The use of violence by the offender

questions.answerNote: Remorse is a recognised mitigating sentencing factor.

questions.stem: Ita punches another person who falls and hits their head. They die as a result of their injuries. Ita is charged with murder. Which element of the offence is difficult to prove to gain a murder conviction?
questions.answerNote: The difficult issue is whether the required intention or recklessness for murder can be proved.

questions.stem: The New South Wales government increased random breath testing operations during the Christmas holidays. This is best described as an example of which of the following?

options.C: A breach of the rule of law

questions.answerNote: Visible RBT increases the perceived risk of detection, a situational strategy.

questions.stem: Which legal concept is demonstrated in this scenario?
questions.answerNote: The conflict concerns the allocation of Commonwealth and state legislative powers.

questions.stem: Which court or tribunal would hear a dispute on this matter and what is the likely outcome?

options.A: High Court — State legislation will be upheld
options.B: Administrative Appeals Tribunal — Both laws are invalid
options.C: International Court of Justice — Commonwealth legislation will be upheld
options.D: High Court — Commonwealth legislation will be upheld

questions.answerNote: The High Court resolves constitutional inconsistency and the valid Commonwealth law prevails.

questions.stem: Why may Legal Aid NOT be granted for a criminal case?

options.A: The Director of Public Prosecutions declines the accused’s request.
options.B: The police determine the offender does not qualify for Legal Aid.
options.C: The accused does not meet the means test requirements.
options.D: The matter is an indictable offence.

questions.answerNote: Eligibility is assessed against means and merits criteria.

questions.stem: Lonnie protests against the Local Council’s decision not to build a skate park. She graffitis the Council offices. What factor affecting criminal behaviour does this best relate to?
questions.answerNote: The act is motivated by protest against a government decision, a political factor.

questions.stem: Ignoring the land rights of Indigenous Peoples represents a failure to protect which human right?
questions.answerNote: Recognition of Indigenous land rights is connected to peoples’ self-determination.

questions.stem: How is Australia best able to uphold international obligations to protect human rights?
questions.answerNote: Domestic legislation gives international obligations effect; D (signing multilateral treaties) is the other plausible answer but signing alone does not uphold obligations.

questions.stem: Granting a defendant bail reflects which fundamental legal principle?

options.A: The right to a fair trial
options.C: The right to trial by peers

questions.answerNote: Bail reflects that an accused is presumed innocent before conviction.

questions.stem: Luke and his friends are instructed by police to leave a public place. Luke is abusive but the officer decides against issuing him with an infringement notice. This is an example of what aspect of police powers?
questions.answerNote: The officer chooses whether to issue a notice, exercising discretion.

questions.stem: Lauren is 16 years old. Two older boys force her, with threats, to steal from a service station. The police apprehend her. Which defence could Lauren raise in this matter?
questions.answerNote: Threats forcing a person to commit an offence may establish duress.

questions.stem: Police charge a 16-year-old with unlicensed driving and a number of traffic offences. In which court will the matter be heard?
questions.answerNote: Traffic offences are dealt with in the Local Court rather than the Children’s Court.

questions.stem: Which legal authority has responsibility for preparing the case for the prosecution of an indictable offence in the District Court?
questions.answerNote: The DPP prepares and conducts prosecutions for serious indictable offences.

questions.stem: Person W provides stolen security access codes to a bank; person X demands money from the teller while holding a gun. Person Y keeps other bank employees in line; person Z drives the getaway vehicle. Who are the principal offenders in this scenario?

options.D: Persons W, X, Y and Z

questions.answerNote: X (gunman) and Y (keeping employees in line, present at scene) are the principals of the first and second degree; W is an accessory before the fact. Z (getaway driver) could arguably be a second-degree principal, but no option is X, Y and Z, so B is the best fit.

questions.stem: Who will determine whether illegally obtained evidence is admissible in the trial of a murder suspect?

options.D: A magistrate in a Committal Conference

questions.answerNote: A murder trial is heard in the Supreme Court, whose judge rules on admissibility.

questions.stem: Sentencing designed to make the accused redress the harm done to society is best reflected by which of the following?
questions.answerNote: Restorative justice (making the offender repair the harm) fits best; C (retribution) is the other plausible answer given the 'harm done to society' wording.

questions.stem: Which of the following best promotes the coordination of the global protection of human rights?
questions.answerNote: Intergovernmental organisations coordinate state cooperation and international frameworks.

questions.stem: A former Australian solider has been charged with war crimes under the Commonwealth Criminal Code, 1995. He was arrested in Sydney. Which body will make a determination in this case?
questions.answerNote: A domestic criminal prosecution of a Commonwealth offence is heard in a competent state court; The ICC is not the trial court.
